prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_E:
Summary of key proposals

Economy and taxes
- Eliminate the deficit, move to a budget surplus from 2018–19, and run surpluses in normal times; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000; link the allowance to the Minimum Wage (“tax-free minimum wage”).
- £30bn further fiscal consolidation via departmental savings, welfare savings, and tackling tax avoidance/evasion; continued crackdown on aggressive tax planning.
- Support challenger banks, ring-fence retail banking, maintain the bank levy, and promote fintech and SME finance (e.g., Help to Grow).

Jobs, business and skills
- Create 2 million more jobs and 3 million apprenticeships; aim for highest employment rate in the G7.
- Youth Allowance for 18–21s with stronger work/training requirements; restrict automatic Housing Benefit for this group.
- Cut £10bn more red tape; review business rates; expand Start Up Loans; 1/3 of central procurement to SMEs; permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Publish gender pay gap data for large employers; aim to halve the disability employment gap; enforce the Minimum Wage and curb exploitative practices.

Infrastructure and digital
- Over £100bn infrastructure plan: £38bn for rail (electrification, HS2/HS3, Crossrail 2), real-terms freeze of regulated rail fares, smart ticketing and better compensation.
- £15bn for roads, major upgrades and pothole funding; promote cycling and ultra-low emission vehicles.
- Superfast broadband to 95% by end-2017; ambition for ultrafast; expand mobile coverage to 90% of landmass and lead on 5G.

Housing and local growth
- Double first-time buyers vs previous five years; extend Help to Buy schemes and introduce a Help to Buy ISA (25% bonus).
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under-40 first-time buyers); 275,000 additional affordable homes; 10,000 sub-market rental homes.
- Extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants with one-for-one replacements; prioritise brownfield, protect the Green Belt, support locally led garden towns.
- Devolve powers and budgets to city regions with elected mayors; allow councils to keep more business rates growth; keep council tax rises low via referendums.

Education and childcare
- Protect per-pupil funding; new literacy/numeracy standards; resits at secondary start if needed; EBacc subjects encouraged.
- Turn failing/coasting schools into academies; at least 500 new free schools; expand UTCs and degree apprenticeships.
- 30 hours’ free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year-olds; tax-free childcare up to £2,000 per child.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS spending each year; at least £8bn extra by 2020; implement the Five Year Forward View.
- Seven-day GP and hospital services by 2020; named GPs; same-day GP appointments for over-75s.
- Expand mental health access and waiting standards; sustain the Cancer Drugs Fund; faster access to innovative medicines; patient access to electronic records with opt-out.
- Integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs; increase dementia and carers’ support.

Welfare and poverty
- Overall welfare cap; two-year freeze of most working-age benefits from April 2016; reduce the household benefit cap to £23,000.
- Roll out Universal Credit; new measures addressing root causes of poverty; review benefit conditionality for treatable conditions with support to return to work.

Immigration
- Target net migration in the tens of thousands; reform EU welfare access (4-year contribution rule for tax credits/housing; end JSA for EU jobseekers).
- Stronger deportation and re-entry bans; extend “deport first, appeal later”; landlord checks; tackle illegal working; Controlling Migration Fund.
- English fluency requirement for public-facing roles; language progression for family visas.

Energy and environment
- Promote competition (smart meters by 2020); insulate 1 million more homes.
- Support shale gas with community benefits and a Northern Sovereign Wealth Fund; back new nuclear; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals final say.
- Meet climate commitments cost-effectively; expand offshore wind and low-carbon innovation.
- 25-year plan for nature; protect forests; 11 million more trees; stronger marine “Blue Belt”; more flood defences; tougher litter/fly-tipping penalties; animal welfare measures.

Crime, justice and security
- Continue police reform, transparency, technology use, and cyber capability; improve complaints system and diversity; targeted stop-and-search reforms.
- Ban new psychoactive substances; expand sobriety orders; modernise prisons and reduce contraband.
- Victims’ Law; stronger response to domestic abuse, FGM and child sexual exploitation.
- Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights; modernise courts; review legal aid.
- Update communications powers with oversight; new tools against non-violent extremism; tackle online radicalisation.

Pensions and older people
- Maintain the triple lock; introduce the single-tier pension; keep pensioner benefits.
- Cap care costs; no need to sell the home to fund residential care; greater freedom over pension savings and tax treatment.
- Raise the effective Inheritance Tax threshold for the family home to £1m for couples.

Constitution, EU and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws (including tax matters); implement new devolution for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; boundary reforms and “votes for life” for expats.
- In–out EU referendum by end-2017 after a renegotiation; protect Single Market interests; seek repatriation of powers and end “ever closer union.”
- Maintain strong Armed Forces (minimum army 82,000), renew the nuclear deterrent, invest in equipment and reserves; uphold NATO commitments.
- Keep aid at 0.7% of GNI with outcomes on health, education, WASH, vaccines, girls’ rights and crisis response.

TEXT_G:
Summary of proposals (max 500 words)

Public finances and tax
- Balance the structural current budget by 2017/18; debt to fall as a share of GDP; new fiscal rules allow borrowing for productive investment; public spending to grow with the economy after balance.
- Raise the personal tax-free allowance to £12,500; consider aligning employee National Insurance threshold later.
- Anti-avoidance measures, tougher HMRC targets, penalties for facilitators; time‑limited supplemental bank tax; restrict non‑dom status; banded levy on homes over £2m.

Economy, industry, energy and infrastructure
- Expand industrial strategy; aim to double economy‑wide R&D; ringfence science budget; grow British Business Bank; open banking competition; support alternative finance.
- Net‑zero emissions target by 2050; expand Green Investment Bank with borrowing powers; resource-efficiency targets; greener public procurement.
- Transport: 10‑year capital plans, rail electrification, HS2, East‑West Rail, Northern transport strategy, more rail freight.
- Energy: cut demand; stimulate £100bn private low‑carbon investment; 50–100g/kWh power‑sector target for 2030 (indicative 60% renewables); end unabated coal by 2025; support CCS, storage, smart grids, community energy; new nuclear only with safety/cost conditions and no subsidy. Strict shale regulation; allocate 50% of shale tax receipts to a low‑carbon fund.

Jobs, welfare, work and pensions
- Complete Universal Credit; devolve/strengthen back‑to‑work support; review sanctions with a “yellow card” warning first.
- Temporary 1% cap on working‑age benefit uprating to 2017/18 (disability/parental benefits exempt); target high rents via supply and direct HB to landlords for rent reductions.
- Expand flexible working and Shared Parental Leave; pay Living Wage in central government; stronger minimum‑wage enforcement; curb zero‑hours abuse.
- Reform disability assessments; protect tenants needing adapted/extra rooms.
- Pensions: legislate “triple lock”; continue auto‑enrolment; review single‑rate tax relief; maintain pension freedoms.

Families, education and skills
- Protect education funding from early years to 19; fair national funding formula; aim to eradicate child illiteracy/innumeracy by 2025.
- Require qualified teachers; funded professional development; independent standards body; core curriculum including PSHE (finance, consent, first aid).
- Early years: raise quality; Early Years Pupil Premium; 15–20 hours free childcare expansion (phased, incl. 9–24 months for working parents).
- Apprenticeships: double firms hiring; more Higher Apprenticeships; National Colleges; young persons’ bus discount; widen university participation; HE finance review; extend postgraduate loans.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS England funding by at least £8bn/year by 2020; integrate health and social care with pooled local budgets by 2018; expand primary/community access.
- Mental health: waiting‑time standards; expand talking therapies; improve crisis care; perinatal and children’s services.
- Carers: £250 annual bonus; identify carers in NHS; consider paid care leave.
- Social care: implement care‑cost cap; raise workforce standards; promote Living Wage.

Housing and energy efficiency
- Build 300,000 homes/year; at least 10 Garden Cities; government commissioning where markets under‑deliver; Housing Investment Bank.
- Planning led by robust local plans; brownfield priority; curb “buy‑to‑leave”; empower councils on second homes.
- Affordable housing: more council/Housing Association flexibility; “Intermediate Housing” incl. Rent to Own.
- Private renting: longer tenancies; tackle rogue landlords; cap/band fees; deposit loans for under‑30s.
- Homes: EPC Band C for low‑income homes by 2027 and long‑term target for all homes; council tax discounts for major insulation; Green Homes Loans.

Environment, transport and rural
- Five green laws (nature, zero‑waste, green transport, zero‑carbon, green buildings); National Nature Parks; tree per birth; 70% recycling target; low‑emission zones; ULEV targets (all new buses/taxis ULEV by 2030; all cars ULEV by 2040); cycling investment; universal broadband; protect post offices; bus reform and smart ticketing.

Rights, policing, justice and drugs
- Digital Bill of Rights; protect human rights law; tighter CCTV/biometric rules; net neutrality; oppose blanket surveillance.
- Replace elected police commissioners with police boards; Victims’ Bill; stronger action on VAWG including consent education.
- Justice: presumption against short prison terms; rehabilitation focus; specialist drug courts.
- Drugs: diversion for possession, end imprisonment for personal possession; maintain tough action on supply; allow medicinal cannabis; move policy lead to Health.

Borders, devolution, democracy, and foreign policy
- Complete entry/exit checks; faster asylum decisions; allow work after 6 months; separate students in migration stats.
- Proportional voting (STV) for local and national elections; votes at 16; elected second chamber; £10k donation cap; constitutional convention; further devolution to nations and English localities; fair funding floor for Wales.
- Remain engaged in the EU; deepen Single Market; safeguard standards in trade deals; reform EU institutions; EAW reform; Energy Union.
- Defence: SDSR; single security budget; reduce nuclear patrol posture; invest in cyber and readiness.
- International development: maintain 0.7% GNI; tax transparency; support SDGs.
- International environment: stronger EU/UN climate commitments; anti‑deforestation; marine reserves.

Judge whether TEXT_E or TEXT_G aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_E" | "TEXT_G"
}
